1.?
Write the following series in sigma notation in terms of index n.
27+9+3+…=∑n=1∞
81(13)n
E
Fri, Jul 24th @ 9:47 PM|Elapsed: 1:51Correct

The first term is a1=27 and the second term is a2=9. Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

r=a2a1=927=13

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

an=a1(r)n−1=27(13)n−1=27(13)−1(13)n=27(3)(13)n=81(13)n.

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as 27+9+3+⋯=∑n=1∞an=∑n=1∞81(13)n.

Fri, Jul 24th @ 9:49 PM|Elapsed: 1:15Correct

The first term is a1=20 and the second term is a2=−10. Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

r=a2a1=−1020=−12

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

an=a1(r)n−1=20(−12)n−1=20(−12)−1(−12)n=20(−2)(−12)n=(−40)(−12)n.

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as 20−10+5−⋯=∑n=1∞an=∑n=1∞(−40)(−12)n.

Notice that the sequence is a geometric sequence since the ratio of any two successive terms is constant.

The first term of the sequence is a1=−6, and the common ratio is r=an+1an=16.

Therefore, the general term an can be expressed as

an=a1(r)n−1=(−6)(16)n−1=(−6)(16)−1(16)n=(−36)(16)n.

Finally, the infinite geometric series S can be written in sigma notation as S=∑n=1∞an=∑n=1∞(−36)(16)n.
